prompt: Company profile: Fleet maintenance garage in Springfield, Missouri; 25 employees; services a municipal-contract bus and truck fleet. Situation: A compliance review found: used motor oil stored in a 300-gallon tank, spent fluorescent lamps boxed in a corner for over a year, a shelf of used aerosol cans, drained oil filters in a drum, and a solvent parts washer whose spent solvent has never had a waste determination. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
# Compliance Obligations Register – Fleet Maintenance Garage (Springfield, MO) | **Compliance Obligation** | **Requirement** | **Regulatory Source** | **Applicability** | **ISO 14001 Clause** | **ISO 45001 Clause** | **Evaluation Method (How/When)** | |---------------------------|-----------------|------------------------|-------------------|----------------------|----------------------|-----------------------------------| | **1. Used Motor Oil Management** | Store used oil in tanks/containers that are: labeled "Used Oil," structurally sound, compatible with contents, closed except when adding/removing oil, and inspected regularly. Must use a permitted transporter/recycler. No RCRA hazardous waste determination required if oil is not mixed with hazardous waste. | 40 CFR 279; Missouri 10 CSR 25-11.279 (adopts federal standards) | Applies to 300-gallon storage tank. Facility is a Used Oil Generator. Must maintain shipment records for 3 years. | 6.1.3 – Environmental compliance obligations | 6.1.3 – Legal requirements for fire/exposure hazards (flammability, slip risks) | **How:** Visual inspections of tank integrity, closure, labeling; review of shipping papers/receipts from recyclers; training records.
**When:** Monthly inspections per SPCC-like best practice; audit annually (9.1.2) and after any spill/release. | | **2. Spent Fluorescent Lamp Universal Waste** | Manage as universal waste: label containers "Universal Waste – Lamps," limit accumulation to **1 year** from first date of generation, ship only to authorized destination facility, maintain shipping records, and train employees on proper handling. Storage >1 year violates 40 CFR 273.35. | 40 CFR 273; Missouri 10 CSR 25-16.273; Missouri DNR guidance | **Immediate violation identified** – lamps stored >1 year. Facility is a Small Quantity Handler of Universal Waste (SQHUW). Must rectify by shipping or manifesting as hazardous waste immediately. | 6.1.3 – Environmental compliance obligations | 6.1.3 – Legal requirements for mercury exposure, broken lamp protocols | **How:** Audit accumulation start dates on containers; verify labeling; review shipping records; inspect storage area for damage.
**When:** **Immediately** to confirm violation correction; then monthly audits (9.1.2) to ensure 1-year limit is met. | | **3. Aerosol Can Universal Waste Management** | May manage intact aerosol cans as universal waste (40 CFR 273.4): label "Universal Waste – Aerosol Cans," store in closed containers, remove only when filling or shipping, no accumulation >1 year, and ship to authorized facility. Must puncture/drain cans only at permitted facility. | 40 CFR 273.4 (EPA 2019 rule); Missouri 10 CSR 25-16.273 | Applies to shelf of used aerosol cans. Must determine if cans are intact/pressurized. If punctured or drained on-site, must evaluate as hazardous waste. | 6.1.3 – Environmental compliance obligations | 6.1.3 – Legal requirements for pressurized containers (explosion, flammability) and chemical exposure | **How:** Inventory count and date-tracking; visual inspection for leaks/damage; review of puncturing equipment permits if used; employee training verification.
**When:** Monthly inventory checks; annual compliance audit (9.1.2); before any puncturing operation. | | **4. Used Oil Filter Management** | Drained oil filters are excluded from hazardous waste IF properly hot-drained or punctured/crushed to remove free-flowing oil. Must store in closed, labeled containers. If not properly drained, must manage as hazardous waste (potentially D018 (lead) or F-listed). | 40 CFR 279.24; Missouri 10 CSR 25-11.279; EPA RCRA Used Oil Filter Guidance | Applies to drum of drained filters. Must verify "properly drained" criteria met. If questionable, must perform hazardous waste determination. | 6.1.3 – Environmental compliance obligations | 6.1.3 – Legal requirements for safe handling (cuts, oil exposure, fire) | **How:** Visual inspection of filters for free-flowing oil; verify drum is closed/labeled; review crushing/draining procedure; waste determination if needed.
**When:** Upon addition to drum; quarterly audits; annual compliance evaluation (9.1.2). | | **5. Hazardous Waste Determination for Spent Solvent** | **IMMEDIATE REQUIREMENT:** Must perform waste determination per 40 CFR 262.11 before further accumulation. If solvent is F-listed (e.g., trichloroethylene, methylene chloride) or exhibits characteristic (D001-043), must manage as hazardous waste under generator rules (likely SQG). Includes labeling, accumulation time limits (180 days SQG), manifesting, training, and contingency plans. | 40 CFR 262.11; Missouri 10 CSR 25-4.262; RCRA Subtitle C | **Critical gap** – no determination made. Facility must immediately sample and analyze or use process knowledge. Assumed to be hazardous waste until proven otherwise. | 6.1.3 – Environmental compliance obligations | 6.1.3 – Legal requirements for chemical exposure (inhalation, dermal), fire, and health risks | **How:** Review lab analysis or process knowledge documentation; verify container labeling ("Hazardous Waste"), accumulation dates, inspector qualifications; review manifest records; audit training.
**When:** **Immediately** upon generation; before any disposal decision; monthly during accumulation; annual comprehensive audit (9.1.2). | | **6. Hazardous Waste Generator Status & Requirements** | If waste determination shows hazardous waste generation >100 kg/month but <1,000 kg/month, register as SQG: obtain EPA ID number, follow 180-day accumulation limits, use manifest system, maintain biennial reports, implement contingency plan, and provide employee training. | 40 CFR 262; Missouri 10 CSR 25-4.262 | Applicability depends on solvent determination and total waste generation rate. Must calculate monthly generation for all waste streams. | 6.1.3 – Environmental compliance obligations | 6.1.3 – Legal requirements for emergency response and employee safety | **How:** Calculate monthly waste generation; review EPA ID status; audit manifests and biennial reports; inspect accumulation areas for compliance with time limits; verify contingency plan and training records.
**When:** Monthly generation calculations; annual compliance audit (9.1.2); within 30 days of any change in waste volume. | | **7. Hazard Communication & Employee Training** | OSHA requires SDSs for all hazardous chemicals (including solvents, oils, aerosols), employee training on hazards and proper handling, and a written Hazard Communication Program. | 29 CFR 1910.1200 (OSHA HAZCOM) | Applies to all employees handling wastes, solvents, oils, aerosols, and lamps (mercury). Must include universal waste and hazardous waste handling procedures. | 6.1.3 – Environmental aspects of chemical management | 6.1.3 – Legal and other OH&S requirements | **How:** Review written program; verify SDS accessibility; audit training records and employee interviews; inspect labeling on secondary containers.
**When:** Upon hire; annually for refresher; when new chemical introduced; during internal audits (9.1.2). | | **8. Emergency Preparedness & Spill Response** | OSHA requires Emergency Action Plan (EAP) for fire/explosion hazards. SPCC-like preparedness needed even if below 1,320-gallon threshold. Must have spill kits, trained responders, and reporting procedures for releases >RQ to NRC/MDNR. | 29 CFR 1910.38 (OSHA EAP); 40 CFR 302 (CERCLA); Missouri 10 CSR 25-6.010 (spill reporting) | Applies to oil storage, solvent, and aerosol cans. Must report spills/releases that exceed Reportable Quantities (e.g., oil >1,000 gallons to water, or any mercury release). | 6.1.3 – Environmental emergency planning | 6.1.3 – OH&S emergency preparedness | **How:** Inspect spill kits and response supplies; review EAP and training records; verify emergency contact lists; conduct mock drills; review spill logs.
**When:** Quarterly drills; annual audit (9.1.2); within 24 hours of any actual spill event. | --- ### **Key Immediate Actions Required:** 1. **Ship fluorescent lamps immediately** – documented violation of 1-year rule. 2. **Perform waste determination on spent solvent** – highest regulatory risk. 3. **Calculate total monthly hazardous waste generation** – determine generator status. 4. **Label all universal waste containers with accumulation start dates.** 5. **Review and update Hazard Communication Program** to include all waste streams. ### **Evaluation Frequency Summary (per 9.1.2):** - **Continuous:** Container closure, labeling, and inspection during operations. - **Monthly:** Visual inspections of storage areas; waste generation calculations. - **Quarterly:** Emergency preparedness drills; training record reviews. - **Annually:** Comprehensive compliance audit of all obligations; management review. - **Trigger-Based:** Upon new waste stream introduction; after any spill/release; within 30 days of regulatory change.
